chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamdani, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A hen is in the house without a rooster; it feeds on chaff and other things and lays eggs without being fertilized by a rooster. What do you say about eating those eggs?' He said: 'If the meat of the egg is edible, there is no harm in eating it; it is halal.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'The Sunnah is in hunting with trained dogs, rather than other beasts of prey.'
This is indicated by what Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'In the book of Ali (peace be upon him):
"Except what you have taught from the hunting beasts, making them trained."

"These are the dogs." The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And when he sends his trained dog after the game, he should mention the name of Allah. If the dog catches it, he should slaughter it, then he may eat it.'
ai.seo_question: Are unfertilized eggs considered halal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of unfertilized eggs, establishing their permissibility based on the general rule that if the meat is edible, the egg is halal. It further details the ritual of hunting with trained dogs (*al-kilab al-mu'allama*), emphasizing the necessity of reciting Allah's name upon release and performing slaughter before consumption, a practice rooted in the Prophetic tradition and linked to the Quranic verse 5:4.
